name: Rio Tinto automation page: a broken link returning corporate boilerplate
title: Rio Tinto automation page: a broken link returning corporate boilerplate
answer: This is not the Rio Tinto automation page. The harvested URL returns a not found error, and the text captured is generic corporate copy about Rio Tinto's global footprint, aluminium, iron ore and shareholder returns. It contains nothing about autonomous haul trucks, drills or operational AI. A reader looking for primary source evidence of automation at Rio Tinto will not find it here, and the claim it is cited for cannot be checked against this text.

sections.body: The source is a page on riotinto.com, the corporate website of Rio Tinto, a metals and mining company. The harvested text is dated 26 September 2026 and opens with the line that the page could not be found, followed by the site's global navigation and standard corporate descriptions. It is therefore not a document about automation at all. What was captured is an error page wrapped in Rio Tinto's general marketing copy, covering the company's countries of operation, its workforce, aluminium, iron ore in Western Australia and its stated aim of delivering returns to shareholders.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The captured text is Rio Tinto's standard corporate copy rather than anything about automation. It states the company's mission to become the world's most valued metals and mining business, for the people who invest in it, the people it works and partners with, and the communities around it. It says Rio Tinto operates in 35 countries where more than 60,000 employees are working to find better ways to provide the materials the world needs. Aluminium is described as tough but malleable, corrosion resistant, recyclable, an excellent conductor of heat and transmitter of electricity, lightweight and infinitely recyclable, and present in jet engines, electric vehicles and mobile phones. Iron ore is described as central to operations in Western Australia, alongside a diverse state presence covering salt, lithium, a diamond legacy and a promising copper gold project. The text twice repeats that the company aims to deliver superior returns to its shareholders while safeguarding the environment and meeting its obligations to wider society. Nothing on the page concerns autonomous haul trucks, autonomous drills or any other automation programme.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives 35 countries of operation and more than 60,000 employees. It lists aluminium's properties and its use in jet engines, electric vehicles and mobile phones, names iron ore as central to Western Australian operations, and mentions salt, lithium, a diamond legacy and a copper gold project in that state. It states twice that the company aims to deliver superior shareholder returns while safeguarding the environment and meeting obligations to wider society. It gives no figures on automation, autonomous trucks or drills.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in mining would come to this source expecting the primary record of Rio Tinto's autonomous haul trucks and drills, and would not find it. As harvested, the page supports no statement about operational AI, so the industry page's claim that Rio Tinto runs the operations proof point cannot be verified from this text. The useful outcome is negative but practical: it shows the citation is currently pointing at a dead or moved URL, and anyone relying on it should locate the live Rio Tinto automation material or another primary source before repeating the claim.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Mining

sections.body: The page is an error page, so it has no author, no publication date and no automation content. It is commercial corporate material from Rio Tinto about itself, written to present the company rather than to document its technology. It covers the company's footprint, commodities and shareholder aims only, and says nothing about how autonomous equipment is deployed, where, at what scale or with what results. The harvest may simply reflect a URL that has been retired or moved, so the absence of automation content here does not show that Rio Tinto publishes none elsewhere.
